description.narrative: EP’s project will for the first time in the DRC place offgrid specific appliances along a strategically identified cold chain anchored by a vertically integrated industrial hub. The ice making will be powered by solar hybrid generation and coupled with an M&E platform delivering base case user data. The data aims to show how refrigeration appliances placed along a fully integrated Paygo, smartmeter connected minigrid supports both the growth of island industrial capacity as well as consumer services and quality of life initiatives. EP agrees with E4A's publications in that cold chain is a vital, yet very untested intervention up to date. EP believes this proposal not only tests ice making based cold chain, but industrialization, distribution, community cold chain as a service chest freezing, and the financing of HH/SME efficient refrigeration appliances. While “cooling as a service” cold chain concepts are unquestionably an exciting concept that EP has centered its energy access approach around, there is still very little research and even fewer test cases on larger ice based chains in the developing world. EP’s project will show the immense innovation that comes from optimization of industrial ice(the hub) operations and distribution centers(spoke) that serve larger numbers of users and are flexible to their evolving needs entrepreneurial and approaches. EP will possess the ability to control the hub asset for maximum efficiency in adjusting to the power and ice needs of the island.

description.narrative: Milestone 2 was our baseline study for our cold chain intervention on Idjwi Island. Full details of our approach can be found in our baseline study attached. The baseline study contained both quantitative and qualitative data collection on Idjwi island to enable analysis and research to establish a strengthened intervention. Equatorial Power’s team utilized our experience in surveying and use of kobo collect tools to create an appropriate survey for analysis based information from earlier high level market research. Equatorial Power have a team of numerators from previous surveys on Idjwi who were then employed to support roll out of quantitative data collection and review of the survey to ensure it made appropriate sense to the community and that they fully understood its requirements. Communities with cold chain intervention potential had previously been identified through our work on idjwi Island and were further validated through meetings with co-operatives and local development organisations. Through the data collection and interviews, our study shows the key locations for cold chain interventions on three key value chains- fish, milk and meat. Mapping of these value chains, understanding their current issues and quantifying cold chain requirement enables us to structure the technical and operational intervention we shall undertake to greater detail to enable impact in line with our M&E Plan. Details of our achievements and findings are given in our baseline study.
